title: Pregnant Students' Rights Act
official_title: To require institutions of higher education to disseminate information on the rights of, and accommodations and resources for, pregnant students, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Hinson (R-IA) with 3 cosponsors; passed the House and was placed on the Senate Legislative Calendar. As an information-disclosure mandate touching abortion-adjacent politics, it is likely to draw Democratic opposition in the Senate, where 60 votes would be needed.
summary: Requires colleges to tell students each year about the rights, accommodations, and resources available to pregnant students who choose to carry a pregnancy to term.
brief: Requires colleges to disseminate information on pregnant students' rights, accommodations, and resources.

top_lines.headline: Pregnant Student Information
subs: Colleges must share pregnant-student rights and resources yearly
Includes campus and community resources and accommodations
Includes how to file a Title IX complaint

items.main: Names the Act the “Pregnant Students' Rights Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Notice of Pregnant Student Rights, Accommodations, and Resources

items.main: Requires colleges in federal student-aid programs to inform students about resources and accommodations for pregnant students carrying a baby to term.
items.detail: Adds subsection (n) to Section 485 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1092). Institutions must give prospective and enrolled students a list of campus and community resources, information on available accommodations, and instructions for filing a Title IX complaint with the Department of Education or the institution. Dissemination must include an annual email, student handbooks, orientations, health or counseling centers, and the institution's website. The subsection does not authorize the Secretary to require additional information or create additional rights.

criticisms.why: Mr. Speaker, I oppose this bill because, among other reasons, the information that is required is incomplete and biased. As written, the Pregnant Students' Rights Act is unfairly limited regarding the information it requires colleges to provide to students and the students it chooses to support. It does not include information about comprehensive family planning resources, and it only supports pregnant students who carry a baby to term. Simply put, the bill fails to support any student with a different pregnancy-related outcome.

gaps: The bill requires distributing information about existing rights but does not create any new accommodations or rights for pregnant students.
It mandates dissemination but specifies no penalty or enforcement mechanism for institutions that fail to comply.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Bonamici
featured_quotes.text: Mr. Speaker, I oppose this bill because, among other reasons, the information that is required is incomplete and biased. As written, the Pregnant Students' Rights Act is unfairly limited regarding the information it requires colleges to provide to students and the students it chooses to support. It does not include information about comprehensive family planning resources, and it only supports pregnant students who carry a baby to term. Simply put, the bill fails to support any student with a different pregnancy-related outcome.

featured_quotes.name: Mrs. Miller
featured_quotes.text: Mr. Speaker, college can be a challenging environment, especially for pregnant women. Many feel forced to choose between motherhood and their education. Nearly 30 percent of all abortions in the United States are performed on women in college. Title IX already protects the right of pregnant women to stay in school. However, many of them face a lack of resources and support. Some even fear punishment and a loss of scholarships simply for carrying their baby to full term while taking classes.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Walberg
featured_quotes.text: to my dear friend and colleague from Georgia, as she has discussed that tragic story with me before, my heart does break. Having experienced that in my own personal family, as well, I understand what she is saying. I am just not capable, I guess, of communicating that this bill is affording all the questions to be answered and all of the issue to be addressed. It also gives pregnant women, who are blessed to be able to continue carrying to completion, the opportunity to also know that their academic opportunity will continue, as well.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Randall
featured_quotes.text: If the sponsor of this bill and the majority party actually believed in supporting student parents, then they would take real action, not just grandstand on the House floor because the March for Life is this weekend. The bill before us today requires the dissemination of incomplete information, but it also comes after House Republicans have worked alongside the Trump regime to dismantle and weaken the Department of Education and protections for students who file complaints around Title IX violations, among other things.

added: Annual college disclosure of pregnant students' rights, accommodations, and resources (new subsection (n) of Higher Education Act Section 485)
